_doc: Session 15: the lore book's narration, one entry per illustrated page (assets/Echoes_of_Caer_Veyr_All_12_Pages/Page_NN.webp, order verified by the printed folios 01-12). Written from THE_CASTLE_REMEMBERS_LORE.md + docs/LORE.md and what each page shows. Markup: each line is one subtitle cue; [tag] = an Eleven v4 audio direction (spoken text only, removed from subtitles); {Display|spoken} = subtitle spelling | pronunciation respelling. tools/lore/gen_lore.mjs voices it, tools/lore/build_lore.py builds public/assets/lore/* + src/data/loreManifest.json.

pages.title: Before the First Crown
lines: [low, reverent narration] Before {Veyr|Vair} had a name… before any crown was forged, or any king was laid in stone… something slept beneath the mountain.
And it remembered.
It kept the shape of stone. The hollow of every chamber. The weight of everything that came near it — and it let nothing go.
Centuries later, the founders of House {Vaelor|Vaylor} broke through into the dark… and found it waiting.
[whispering] They called it the Crownheart.

pages.title: The Blood That Opened Stone
lines: The first rulers did not understand what they had found. They learned only this… it answered to blood.
So they gave it theirs. Before the ancient ring, the first king opened his palm… and the stone drank.
Doors that were never built for human hands swung open. Hidden chambers breathed again. Preserved memories obeyed.
And a promise became a belief… and the belief became law.
[reverently] The castle remembers its rightful king.

pages.title: A Kingdom Built on Memory
lines: {Caer Veyr|Kair Vair} rose above the Crownheart. Walls became towers. Towers became halls. And generations passed beneath its banners.
Every coronation deepened the binding. Every royal rite drew the castle closer to the blood.
[lower, thoughtful] House {Vaelor|Vaylor} believed it owned the Crownheart's memory…
[whispering] It never understood… that the Crownheart was learning House {Vaelor|Vaylor}.

pages.title: The Last Days of Veyr
lines: Under King Aldren {Vaelor|Vaylor}, a long war came home at last. The fires of the siege burned from one horizon to the other.
Behind the gates, the people of {Veyr|Vair} crowded into the halls… and waited for the end.
[hushed, urgent] But the king did not wait. By candlelight, deep in the royal archives, he searched the records of his fathers…
[slowly, with restrained awe] and he found a possibility. The whole of {Caer Veyr|Kair Vair}… held forever, at one chosen moment.

pages.title: The Price of Forever
lines: [grave] But the Crownheart could not hold so much without living resonance. It needed lives, bound into its memory… thousands of them.
Aldren looked upon the people sheltering inside his walls… and he chose them.
To him, losing the kingdom was a greater crime than sacrificing those who lived in it.
[quiet dread] The deepest chambers were sealed. Guards turned to face inward. Servants vanished in the night…
and the work began.

pages.title: A House Divided
lines: Some at court learned what the king intended… and tried to stop him.
[intense] And {Caer Veyr|Kair Vair} turned against itself — soldiers of {Veyr|Vair} cutting down soldiers of {Veyr|Vair}, beneath the same banners.
In the chaos, a child was taken from the castle. Royal blood, never acknowledged… never marked… never bound by the rites.
[whispering] A servants' door. A hand in the dark. The moon over the walls.
[reflective] That forgotten branch of House {Vaelor|Vaylor} would endure… long after the ruin.

pages.title: The Sundering
lines: At the height of the siege, Aldren descended to the Crownheart and began the ritual.
The bells of {Caer Veyr|Kair Vair} rang out… and the ritual was interrupted.
[rising dread] The Crownheart failed to hold one moment. The ancient ring broke apart, and its memory tore in two —
the castle as it stood before the catastrophe… and the ruin it would become, generations later.
[heavy, final] Two remembered states, locked in the same stone.
[whispering] This was the Sundering.

pages.title: Those Who Could Not Leave
lines: Generations passed. The road to {Caer Veyr|Kair Vair} vanished beneath the forest, and ordinary life abandoned it.
[low] But not everything left. Thousands of human imprints remained within the Crownheart… the Echoes.
Some still remember who they were.
[sorrowful] Others keep watch at doors that no longer matter… repeating an order, long after its meaning died.
[whispering] And sometimes, in windows that fell centuries ago… a torch is burning.

pages.title: The Uncrowned
lines: The child who escaped did not die. Her line went on, far from {Veyr|Vair} — a worn crest, a half-forgotten name, a warning about a castle no one should enter.
And from that unbound line came a woman… with a claim to the ruin.
[measured] {Vaelor|Vaylor} blood, without the completed binding. Connected to the castle… yet not imprisoned by it.
She came to reclaim a stolen inheritance.
[whispering] She was the Uncrowned.

pages.title: Which Memory Will Answer?
lines: Inside, the Echoes rose against her. And when they fell, they released the resonance trapped within them… and her blood could gather it.
[intense, building] With that power, she could force the castle to choose… and another memory would answer.
Rubble gathered itself back into walls. Torches burned where only moonlight had been.
[slowly] She did not travel through history.
The castle changed… around her.

pages.title: What the Stones Confessed
lines: [low, uneasy] But the castle's two memories did not agree.
A door that stood sealed in the Past… lay broken outward in the Present. The wounds were in the wrong places.
The stones told a different history. The people of {Caer Veyr|Kair Vair} had not been defending their king.
[sorrowful] They had been trying to escape him.
[grave, restrained] The siege was real. But the catastrophe… was Aldren's.

pages.title: The Last Crown
lines: [low, ominous] Aldren did not die in the Sundering. He remained… fused with the Crownheart, until king, castle and memory could no longer be told apart.
The Last Crown.
He still believes {Veyr|Vair} can be saved. And her unbound blood… might finish his ritual.
[slowly, with weight] She had come to claim her inheritance.
[whispering] Now she had to ask…
should this inheritance survive at all?
